patients.summary: University student and track runner who joins the practice healthy at 20, is diagnosed with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy after collapsing at practice in 2023 and started on metoprolol, has recurrent syncope with a recorded pause in 2024, and in 2026 has an emergency craniotomy for a traumatic epidural hematoma after an unhelmeted motorcycle crash, with full recovery.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
20 y/o M, college student, heading into his junior year, runs distance and middle distance on the track team. Wanted one doctor he could text while at school. Last primary care was his pediatrician in Connecticut, records release signed today.

No complaints. No chronic problems, never hospitalized, no surgeries. No meds, no supplements. NKDA.

FH: father died suddenly at 41. Pt doesn't know the cause, was never told details. No other family history he can name today.
SH: lives in campus housing during the year, home in Deerfield in the summers. Never smoked, no vaping. Drinks occasionally at social events, a few drinks a month. No drugs.

ROS negative, specifically no chest pain, palpitations, fainting or trouble keeping up at practice.

Exam: vitals as charted. Lean, well appearing. HEENT clear. Neck supple, no adenopathy. Heart regular rate and rhythm, S1 S2 normal, no murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses. Extremities without edema, pulses 2+ and symmetric. Skin clear. Neuro grossly normal.

PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 2.

A/P
1. Health maintenance, healthy 20 y/o. One-time HIV and hep C screening today, plus CBC, CMP and lipids as a baseline. Vaccine history pending pediatric records; will catch up flu and COVID in the fall.
2. Family history of sudden death in father, cause unknown. Asked him to find out what he can from family.

RTC one year, or sooner as needed. Gave him the practice cell number.

documents.body: Rowan, all of your labs from Monday look normal: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, cholesterol, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens are both negative. Nothing to change. Good luck with the semester.

orders.reason: Exertional collapse with chest tightness, systolic murmur, father with sudden death at 41

documents.title: Office Visit - Collapse
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Texted me last night, I asked him to come in first thing.

S: Yesterday afternoon during interval repeats at indoor practice he felt a brief tight feeling in his chest, then the next thing he knew he was on the track with teammates and the coach over him. Teammates say he was out only briefly, no shaking reported, didn't bite his tongue, no incontinence. Came around quickly and was clear. Coach wanted him to go to the ED; he declined and walked back to the dorm. Fine since. No chest pain now, no palpitations he noticed. Never happened before. Ate and drank normally that day.

No meds. NKDA.
FH: father died suddenly at 41, still doesn't know more.

O: Vitals as charted. Well, comfortable. Heart regular, there is a soft systolic murmur at the left lower sternal border that I did not hear in August. No gallop. Lungs clear. No edema. Neuro nonfocal.
ECG in office: NSR, normal intervals, no LVH, no Q waves, no ST-T changes. Normal.

A/P: Syncope with exertion, preceded by chest tightness, new murmur, and a father who died suddenly young. Normal ECG doesn't reassure me enough. Urgent cardiology referral today for consult and echo. No running, lifting or hard exertion until cardiology sees him; he'll tell his coach and I'll write a note. If anything recurs, chest pain, palpitations or near-fainting, he goes straight to the ED, not to me.
Discussed with him for a while, he understands why.

documents.title: Athletics note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
To the athletics department:

Rowan Doherty was seen in our office today. He should not participate in practice, competition or strength training until he has completed a cardiology evaluation and we provide written clearance.

Primary care physician

documents.title: Cardiology referral scheduled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Cardiology referral faxed with today's note and ECG. Their scheduler had an opening for new consult Mon 3/13 at 1:00, echo same day. Called pt, confirmed he can make it, he'll drive home from school the night before. Insurance is his mother's plan, card on file current, no referral auth needed for specialist per plan.

medications.drug: 24 HR metoprolol succinate 50 MG Extended Release Oral Tablet

reports.text: Complete 2D, M-mode, color and spectral Doppler study. Left ventricle normal in cavity size. Asymmetric hypertrophy of the interventricular septum, maximal septal wall thickness 21 mm; posterior wall 10 mm. Left ventricular systolic function hyperdynamic, LVEF 70% by visual estimate. Systolic anterior motion of the anterior mitral leaflet. Resting LVOT peak gradient 38 mmHg, increasing to 64 mmHg with Valsalva. Mitral and aortic valves structurally normal. Tricuspid and pulmonic valves normal. Right ventricle normal in size and function. Atria normal in size. No pericardial effusion. IVC normal with normal respiratory variation.
reports.conclusion: Asymmetric septal hypertrophy with systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve and dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (resting 38 mmHg, 64 mmHg with Valsalva), consistent with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. LVEF 70%. No structural valvular abnormality.

documents.title: Cardiology Consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outpatient cardiology consultation
Date of visit: 03/13/2023
Referring: primary care physician
Reason: syncope during exercise

Dear colleague,

Thank you for asking me to see Rowan, a 20-year-old university student and track athlete. On 3/2 during an interval workout he had a short-lived sensation of chest tightness and then lost consciousness, coming around quickly on the track. He had no prior episodes. He has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. No known drug allergies.

Family history: he spoke with his family this past week. His father died suddenly at 41; the family has understood it as a cardiac death. A paternal uncle carries a diagnosis of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

Social: never smoker, occasional alcohol on weekends, no drug use. Full-time student.

Vital signs were stable today. On exam he is a fit young man in no distress. JVP not elevated. There is a systolic murmur at the left lower sternal border. Lungs clear. No peripheral edema.

Echocardiogram today shows asymmetric septal hypertrophy (21 mm septum, 10 mm posterior wall) with systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve and a resting outflow gradient of 38 mmHg that rises to 64 mmHg with Valsalva. Ejection fraction 70%. The valves themselves are structurally normal.

Impression: Obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, presenting with exertional syncope.

Plan:
1. Start metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily. Prescription sent.
2. He should stay out of competitive running and strenuous exertion. We talked at length about what that means for his season; light recreational activity is fine.
3. Stay well hydrated and avoid dehydration and heavy alcohol use, both of which worsen obstruction.
4. Return to clinic in one year, sooner for any recurrent symptoms.

Allergies: NKDA
Medications at end of visit: metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily

Sincerely,
Outpatient cardiology

documents.title: cardiology
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, saw the cardiologist monday. They said hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and put me on metoprolol 50. Can you do the refills from here on or do I go through them? Also I'm off the team for the season so you don't need to send anything else to the coach

documents.title: RE: cardiology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Rowan, I got the consult letter yesterday and read it through. I'm sorry about the season. Yes, I'm happy to handle refills; just let us know when you're getting low. Let's get you in here in about a month to see how you're doing on the metoprolol and talk through any questions.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u new dx obstructive HCM (cardiology 3/13, septum 21 mm, LVOT 38 resting / 64 Valsalva, EF 70%).

Taking metoprolol succinate 50 every morning, hasn't missed doses. No further passing out, no chest tightness, no palpitations. Walking around campus fine. Off the track team, doing some light swimming and walking, within what cardiology allowed. Taking it fairly well, a little flat about losing the season but sleeping and eating ok, not depressed. Has been reading about HCM, we went over questions about genetics in the family and what it means for his future.

Meds: metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily. NKDA.
FH now clarified: father SCD at 41, paternal uncle with HCM.

Exam: vitals as charted. Heart regular, systolic murmur LLSB. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P
1. Obstructive HCM, on metoprolol, tolerating. Continue. Refills through us. Cardiology annual f/u next March. Reinforced: fluids, no heavy drinking, no hard exertion, ED for any recurrence.
2. Health maintenance: physical in August.
Rx metoprolol succinate 50 mg #90 with 3 refills sent to his pharmacy.

documents.title: Pharmacy refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy called to confirm the 90 day supply on metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg, pt switched to the pharmacy near home for summer. Transfer from the campus pharmacy completed by them. Refills remain on file. No action needed from PCP.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. 21 y/o M, senior year starting next week.

Obstructive HCM dx 3/2023, on metoprolol succinate 50 daily, no missed doses. No syncope or near syncope since March, no chest pain, no palpitations, no exercise intolerance with walking and easy swimming. Stays out of competitive sports.

Meds: metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.
SH: no tobacco or vaping, alcohol a few drinks a month at most, no drugs. Uses a seatbelt.
FH: father SCD 41; paternal uncle HCM.

ROS otherwise negative.
PHQ-9 2. AUDIT-C 2.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well appearing. HEENT normal, TMs clear. Neck supple, no thyromegaly or adenopathy. Heart regular, systolic murmur LLSB, unchanged. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. GU deferred. Extremities: no edema. Skin: no concerning lesions. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P
1. Obstructive HCM, stable on metoprolol. Continue. Cardiology f/u due March.
2. Health maintenance. CBC and BMP today. Flu and COVID this fall, he'll come in when home in October. Tdap last 2014, due next year. HIV/HCV done 2022.
RTC 1 yr.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Rowan, your blood count and chemistry panel from Monday are normal, including potassium and kidney function. Have a good start to senior year.
